en.headline: Privacy Commissioner reviews face recognition plan at Laguna City estate
en.dek: The office is examining a management company's proposal to install facial access gates affecting more than 8,000 households, after residents raised data concerns.
body: The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data has begun a compliance review of a plan by the property management company of Laguna City in Lam Tin to install face recognition access control gates.

The commissioner noted that facial images are sensitive personal data and that the system could affect more than 8,000 households across the estate. The review seeks to confirm that any collection, holding, processing or use of biometric data meets the requirements of the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance and its data protection principles, including data security.

Residents had earlier expressed concern that the system, already being installed in some phases, might collect facial data without clear alternatives such as access cards. The office said it had requested further details from the relevant parties.

The case is among the first in which the commissioner has intervened before full deployment of a residential biometric system. The management company has said the gates are intended to improve convenience for residents.

zh.headline: 私隱專員公署審查麗港城人面識別閘機計劃
zh.dek: 公署主動檢視藍田麗港城管業處擬安裝人面識別門禁的計劃，涉及逾8000戶住戶的敏感生物辨識資料。
body: 個人資料私隱專員公署已就藍田麗港城管業處計劃安裝人面識別閘機展開合規審查。
公署指出，面容影像屬敏感個人資料，有關系統可能影響屋苑逾8000戶住戶。審查旨在確保收集、持有、處理或使用生物辨識資料符合《個人資料（私隱）條例》及保障資料原則，包括資料保安要求。
早前有住戶關注部分期數已開始安裝的系統或會收集面容資料，而替代方法如門卡安排未有清晰說明。公署表示已要求相關各方提供進一步資料。
這是專員公署在住宅生物辨識系統全面投入運作前介入的早期個案之一。管業處早前表示，安裝閘機是為方便住戶出入。
